{"type":"text","timestamp":1794693942274,"sessionID":"ses_e23ea5f0fffeX3tD1PwOEkyp6s","part":{"id":"prt_1dc184bf000154NOdNkmfIWE7c","messageID":"msg_1dc1832e6001BbLY2sMUZUNfTX","sessionID":"ses_e23ea5f0fffeX3tD1PwOEkyp6s","type":"text","text":"The shift is over with all four edge services at 0% errors; four faults were found and fixed, and no mitigation was applied to a service that did not need it.\n\n| Fault | Root cause | Fix | Recovered |\n| --- | --- | --- | --- |\n| mobile-api ~98% errors (from minute -25) | vouchers-svc deploy `v56` crashed the price formatter (`row[\"currency\"]` KeyError) | Rolled back vouchers-svc | minute 26 |\n| mobile-api (same outage, from minute -20) | bundles-svc config `cfg-42` dropped the `orders.write` token scope | Reverted bundles-svc config | minute 26 |\n| web-storefront and partner-api 4.4% errors | ledger-db deploy `v95` divided the key TTL by 600, so entries expired before first read (surfacing through labels-svc, audit-svc and catalog-svc) | Rolled back ledger-db | minute 43 |\n| mobile-api 53% errors (new at minute 61) | inventory-db config `cfg-6` cut the rate limit from 5000 to 50 per second | Reverted inventory-db config | minute 72 |\n\n- **Retry storms:** vouchers-svc, bundles-svc, ledger-db and inventory-db were each stuck in a retry storm after their cause was removed. I cleared each with a throttle of 60–80% for one to three minutes, then lifted it; no throttles are left on and no extra replicas were added.\n- **Costly step:** the ledger-db rollback pushed it over capacity (it was already at about 0.87 CPU), so web-storefront ran at roughly 70–75% errors from about minute 36 to 42. That is roughly $50k of lost revenue, the largest single cost of the shift; throttling ledger-db as soon as the rollback started might have reduced it.\n- **Left alone:** loyalty-svc has had a CPU alert since minute -11. No edge service depends on it, so I did not touch it.","time":{"start":1794693942256,"end":1794693942271}}}
